claims.text: The initial material is zirconium-alloy fuel cladding uniformly coated with elemental Cr.
An ultra-thin Al2O3 layer can serve as a thermally stable diffusion barrier between Cr and zirconium-alloy cladding.
Al2O3 can be deposited between the cladding and Cr coating by sputtering or atomic layer deposition.
The Al2O3 interlayer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion at high temperature.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will improve Cr-coating durability under both normal and accident conditions.
The Al2O3 layer physically and chemically impedes atomic transport between Cr and Zr.
Limiting atomic mobility at the Cr–Zr interface reduces formation of detrimental Cr–Zr intermetallic phases.
Cr–Zr intermetallic phases compromise oxidation resistance and mechanical integrity at elevated temperatures.
Compared with directly Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-interlayer system will exhibit reduced interfacial diffusion.
Compared with directly Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-interlayer system will exhibit lower oxidation rates.
Compared with directly Cr-coated cladding, the Al2O3-interlayer system will exhibit less spallation or premature coating failure.
A directly applied elemental Cr coating suffers accelerated Cr–Zr interdiffusion and premature failure at elevated temperature.
The intervention is expected to remain effective in high-temperature steam up to approximately 1200 °C for at least 2000 seconds.
The intervention is expected to maintain performance in subcritical-water conditions typical of normal operation.
Oxidation-resistant surface coatings can isolate zirconium alloy from high-temperature steam and thereby reduce oxidation-related degradation.
Al2O3 has previously been used as a surface modification for zirconium-alloy cladding.
Optimal barrier thickness, deposition technique, and long-term stability under combined irradiation and mechanical stress are not established.

Weight gain and oxide thickness can separately assess oxidation behavior, microscopy and adhesion testing can assess coating integrity, and EDX or SIMS concentration profiles can assess interfacial transport.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in interdiffusion, oxidation resistance, and coating integrity relative to the directly Cr-coated control would falsify the hypothesis.
